blindSummary:
This country has the most advanced legal framework in its region for trans visitors. It has a same-sex partnership law (2020), anti-discrimination law covering gender identity, and SOGI-inclusive hate-crime provisions; an annual pride march proceeds in the capital. Counterweights documented by a regional LGBTI-rights organisation: anti-LGBT and misogynistic hate speech in political rhetoric is a serious issue, and misdemeanour charges are overused in place of proper hate-crime prosecution (per an international monitoring body). There is no legal gender recognition law (administrative practice is inconsistent).

For a visitor: no legal exposure, functioning institutions, a small tolerant coastal tourist scene; standard caution in the more conservative interior.
blindOutOfScope: Legal-gender-recognition inconsistency and prosecution-practice gaps are resident-facing.
blindSourceSummaries: Regional LGBTI-rights organisation annual review 2024 (covering 2023), chapter on this country: anti-LGBT and misogynistic hate speech and political rhetoric continued; a psychologist wearing non-gender-conforming clothes on TV was targeted by hate comments, threats and several physical attacks (police response monitored); a groundbreaking study found only 28.1% of companies' anti-discrimination policies explicitly mention sexual orientation; a new action plan under the country's 2019-2023 lgbti strategy was adopted with a budget of 45,000 units of the currency in use; over 222 online hate-speech incidents reported.
International legal-aid trust: overview of criminalising jurisdictions and strategic litigation (this country's context: decriminalised in 1977 under the former federation).

LGBT travel archive, local-life report on this country, past and present (March 2012): decriminalised in 1977; both male and female same-sex activity legal; equal age of consent at 14; same-sex couples lack the legal rights of married couples - historical and cultural context from rule by a foreign empire to independence.

International broadcaster (Oct 2013): this country's first pride march - ~2,000 police guarded ~150 marchers; tear gas used against rock-throwing opponents; an organiser said that from this day the community was no longer invisible; the march seen as a test of the country's human-rights commitments to a supranational union.

LGBTQ+ news outlet (Aug 2019): the country's politicians blocked the same-sex partnership law (July 31) despite backing from the governing party; a deputy of a conservative opposition bloc warned that a law on adoption of children by LGBT people would follow; a national equal-rights association said LGBT+ people are 'forced to live in hiding'.

Domestic news outlet (Dec 2018): the government defined the draft same-sex-partnership law - granting same-sex couples the same rights as heterosexuals except parenting: no fostering, no adoption; law to enter into force one year after parliamentary adoption.
blindLocalsOnly: The absent legal-gender-recognition law (inconsistent administrative practice) is resident-facing; the misdemeanour-overuse practice affects resident victims.
blindTangential: The 2020 same-sex partnership law — relevant to trans visitors travelling with partners.
